    AI Overview
    Marion County, Florida, established in 1844 and seated in Ocala, is a North Central Florida region known as the "Horse Capital of the World®," containing over 35% of the state's horses. With a 2020 population of 375,908, it is a rapidly growing area featuring major attractions like Silver Springs State Park and the Ocala National Forest. The area has a diverse population, with roughly 61% White and 30% Black residents, a median household income of $61,010, and a 14.3% poverty rate. 
    Key Aspects of Marion County, FL: 
    • Major Cities & Areas: The county includes Ocala (county seat), The Villages, Belleview, Dunnellon, and unincorporated communities like Ocala National Forest.
    • Economy: Often called the "Horse Capital of the World®," the county houses numerous thoroughbred farms.
    • Demographics & Housing: As of 2026 data, there are approximately 189,627 total housing units, with 139,348 single-family homes. The population is diverse, featuring a high percentage of families.
    • Cost of Living: The median household income is approximately $61,010.
    • Education: The school system operates at 93% capacity. Educational opportunities include the Marion County Community Technical and Adult Education Center and Taylor College.
    • Recreation: Key natural spots include Silver Springs State Park and Rainbow Springs.
    • Public Services: The Marion County Sheriff's Office handles law enforcement and offers various community resources. 
    Note: The results indicate multiple "Marion County" locations in the US, but the above information specifically pertains to Marion County, Florida.

    How many Marion counties are in the US?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    There are 17 counties named Marion in the United States, mostly named after Revolutionary War General Francis Marion, the "Swamp Fox". These counties are located in Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Mississippi, Missouri, Ohio, Oregon, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, and West Virginia.
